title: S015 — Incremental propagation / affected-fixpoint derivation
description: Test whether Somnium can update its semantic fixpoint incrementally after an intervention, recomputing only the affected dependency region, while remaining exactly equivalent to the full propagateJudgments().
result_summary: HOLD. Measured the affected region per intervention type and tested whether a naive reverse-dependency closure is a sound over-approximation for a scoped recompute. Locality: setFact 7%, retractFact 3-10%, addEdge 1-2%, severEdge 5-6% of the model (LOCAL); forceEvent 23-31%, negateEvent 29-38% (WIDE, because event status cascades through REQUIRES chains). But the closure is NOT sound: 1-3 nodes outside it changed per intervention kind on both canons (verrin and ordos). Cause: Phase B unfoundedSet is GLOBAL (a change can reclassify a bootstrap cycle not reverse-reachable), and Phase A's sticky rule makes outcomes order-dependent across the whole node set. A correct incremental path needs a stronger over-approximation or explicit full fallback. Correctness was never compromised: the full propagateJudgments remained the reference, no second semantic engine, nothing shipped. Long-horizon and scaling not run because the correctness gate failed.
next_experiment: propagation observability - instrument propagateJudgments to emit its own per-stage re-evaluation set, mirroring S011's fold-state delta, so an incremental path can invalidate exactly what the reference touches.
limitations: Only seed canons + 200-step random histories tested.
The invalidation model does not model the global unfoundedSet reclassification - exactly where it fails.
No long-horizon or scaling measurements (correctness gate failed).
